claims.text: What the strip looks like Often looks like an anterior STEMI.
Aspects (abnormal in red) ST segment: no ECG criteria can safely tell it apart from STEMI in the ED; if in doubt, activate the STEMI protocol
claims.quote: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is difficult to distinguish from STEMI in the ED, and no ECG criteria can be safely used to differentiate between the two conditions. If in doubt, you should activate your local code STEMI protocol

claims.text: T waves (evolving phase): deep T-wave inversions
claims.quote: Deep T-wave inversions and marked QT prolongation in evolving phase
Deep T-wave inversions and marked QT prolongation in evolving phase

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) What it is: a transient wall motion abnormality of the LV apex with severe emotional or physical stress, usually resolving completely
claims.quote: Transient wall motion abnormality of the left ventricular apex associated with severe emotional or physical stress that usually resolves completely

claims.text: Mechanism: an acute stress response causes a catecholamine surge; the sympathetic activation causes microvascular spasm
claims.quote: An acute stress response leads to a catecholamine surge Ensuing sympathetic nervous system activation causes microvascular spasm.

claims.text: Clinical context: emotional stressor, post-menopausal woman, apical ballooning on echo, clean coronaries on angiography
claims.quote: Clinical context matters: emotional stressor, post-menopausal woman, apical ballooning on echo, clean coronaries on angiography

claims.text: 90% of cases occur in post-menopausal women, usually after sudden emotional stress; in men it is more often physical stress
claims.quote: 90% of cases worldwide occur in post-menopausal women, usually associated with sudden emotional stress. Cases in men are more likely to be associated with physical stress

claims.text: Mayo criteria: transient LV apical/mid dyskinesis; wall motion beyond one coronary territory; no culprit coronary stenosis > 50%; new ECG changes (ST elevation or T inversion) or a moderate troponin rise; no pheochromocytoma or myocarditis
claims.quote: Mayo Clinic diagnostic criteria Transient dyskinesis of the LV apical and/or midsegments Regional wall motional abnormalities beyond a single epicardial vascular distribution Absence of coronary artery stenosis > 50% of culprit lesion New ECG changes (ST elevation or T wave inversion) or moderate troponin rise Absence of phaeochromocytoma and myocarditis

claims.text: Angiography is required to tell it from a STEMI definitively
claims.quote: The presentation often mimics a STEMI and angiography is required to definitively differentiate the two conditions

claims.text: Symptoms Ischemic chest pain, ECG changes, ± raised cardiac enzymes, with normal coronary arteries on angiography
claims.quote: Produces ischaemic chest pain, ECG changes +/- elevated cardiac enzymes in patients with normal coronary arteries on angiography

claims.text: Treatment Largely supportive; LV function usually returns on its own within 21 days
claims.quote: Treatment is largely supportive, and LV function usually spontaneously returns within 21 days of onset

claims.text: Anticoagulate patients with large areas of hypokinesis (high risk of cerebral thromboembolism)
claims.quote: Anticoagulation should be initiated in patients with large areas of cardiac hypokinesis, as they are at high risk of cerebrovascular thromboembolic events

claims.text: Better prognosis than a STEMI with a similar ECG, but not benign
claims.quote: Takotsubo has a better prognosis than STEMIs with a similar ECG but it is certainly not benign

claims.text: At least one-third have some LVOT obstruction; these patients usually have more severe disease and a poorer prognosis
claims.quote: In at least one-third of cases, there is a degree of underlying left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, which increases LV workload, worsening sympathetic nervous system activation and apical dyskinesis. These patients usually have more severe disease and a poorer prognosis
